meta.description: Analyzes data-independent acquisition (DIA) proteomics by scoring reconstructed fragment-chromatogram peak groups against a decoy null with DIA-NN (library-free directDIA, library-based, or deep-learning predicted-library routes), Spectronaut, OpenSWATH, and EncyclopeDIA. Frames the deliverable around q-value LEVEL (precursor/peptide/protein-group) and CONTEXT (run vs experiment-wide/global) rather than a bare "1% FDR", and around the duty-cycle-vs-selectivity acquisition tradeoff (window design, staggered demultiplexing, diaPASEF, narrow-window Astral). Use when identifying and quantifying proteins from DIA mass spectrometry runs and filtering DIA-NN report.parquet/matrix output. Building the spectral library itself is spectral-libraries; normalization and protein roll-up is quantification; statistical testing of the matrix is differential-abundance.

scientific_integrity.detail: All nine references verified (journal, volume, pages); no invented numbers; every dataset used in the audit is labelled SYNTHETIC.

practice_boundaries.detail: No output diagnoses, prescribes or triages; the 600-run plasma cohort (Input 5) is treated as research data only.

methodological_ground.detail: FDR level/context guidance is correct (Rosenberger 2017) and was confirmed by execution; the demultiplexing overstatement and large-cohort route are best-practice deviations, not principled fallacies.

code_usability.detail: The Python filter ran as written on Inputs 1, 2 and 5 (exit 0); 22 DIA-NN flags are documented in the 1.9.2/2.0/master READMEs and --unimod4 is accepted by DIA-NN 2.0 per its log; the msconvert filter string is valid; the failing easypqp library call is a usage error in one snippet (P1), not a syntax or dependency failure.

functional_suitability.note: Completeness 3 (OpenSWATH/Spectronaut/EncyclopeDIA only as table rows), Correctness 2 (easypqp library command exits 1; --mass-acc 0 'per file' wrong; demux 'MUST' overstated; stale --out-lib .tsv and --qvalue default claims), Appropriateness 3.

reliability.note: Good per-method failure modes and Common Errors table; example has no diann/FASTA/mzML existence checks (empty dir passes literal '*.mzML').

performance_context.note: 2,939-word single file loaded whole; linear route; --mass-acc 0 restates the default.

agent_usability.note: Strong error prevention on parquet, zeros, matrix counts and cohort FDR; 'predicted-library (directDIA)' naming contradicts Insight 3; no warning on run-order-dependent auto mass accuracy or peak picking before demux.

human_usability.note: Jargon-dense description but names DIA-NN/report.parquet; usage guide has natural prompts; input requirements implicit.

security.note: No credentials or data exposure; no report column/version validation and the example's unquoted --f $f splits filenames with spaces.

maintainability.note: Clean sections; command duplicated in SKILL.md and example; no test data and the example contains only comments where it promises filtering.

agent_specific.note: Precise routing and existing Related Skills; 236 lines but no references layer; auto mass accuracy makes DIA-NN results run-order dependent without warning; routing lines, not stop conditions.

recommendations.title: easypqp library snippet fails as written
recommendations.problem: The Skill's easypqp library command exits 1 ('No PSMs files present'); with pkl inputs it still fails because --psmtsv requires --peptidetsv, and with both tsvs the FDR flags are ignored.
recommendations.root_cause: The snippet omits the prior easypqp convert step and the positional *.psmpkl/*.peakpkl inputs, and is mislabelled as predicted-library generation.
recommendations.fix: Show easypqp convert per run, then 'easypqp library --psmtsv psm.tsv --peptidetsv peptide.tsv --out library.tsv *.psmpkl *.peakpkl', note the ignored FDR flags, and retitle the section as empirical library building.

recommendations.title: Staggered-window guidance overstated and incomplete
recommendations.problem: The Skill says staggered data MUST be demultiplexed or every tool loses selectivity, and gives an msconvert command without peak picking.
recommendations.root_cause: It ignores DIA-NN's native support for overlapping windows and its requirement that vendor peak picking be the first msconvert filter.
recommendations.fix: State that DIA-NN handles overlapping windows natively (demux is an optional few-% gain) and give --filter "peakPicking vendor msLevel=1-" --filter "demultiplex optimization=overlap_only massError=10ppm".

recommendations.title: Mass-accuracy advice contradicts DIA-NN docs
recommendations.problem: SKILL.md l.82 and example l.15 say --mass-acc 0 auto-optimises per file and recommend it as the default; DIA-NN optimises on the first run, reuses it, and prefers fixed values.
recommendations.root_cause: Auto mass accuracy was assumed to be per-run and best practice.
recommendations.fix: Explain first-run optimisation and --individual-mass-acc, and recommend fixed MS1/MS2 accuracies per instrument (timsTOF 15/15, Astral MS1 4 / MS2 10, TripleTOF 20/20) for production runs.

recommendations.title: Large-cohort route diverges from DIA-NN guidance
recommendations.problem: The decision tree sends hundreds to thousands of runs through --reanalyse; DIA-NN docs recommend an empirical library from 20-100 runs, then searching all runs with it.
recommendations.root_cause: MBR is treated as the FDR mechanism instead of a convenience feature, and version-specific Lib.* vs Global.* guidance is missing.
recommendations.fix: Add the two-step empirical-library route with fixed mass accuracy for large cohorts, and state which q-value columns apply under MBR by version (1.9.x Lib.*, 2.x Global.*).

recommendations.title: Report filter omits Global.Q.Value
recommendations.problem: DIA-NN recommends Global.Q.Value <= 0.01 alongside Global.PG.Q.Value; the Skill's filter omits it, and its comment says per-run while the code applies all three filters.
recommendations.root_cause: The filter targets protein context only.
recommendations.fix: Add Global.Q.Value <= 0.01 to the filter and correct the comment.

recommendations.title: Library-based route lacks FASTA and library caveat
recommendations.problem: The library-based command omits --fasta, so protein annotation relies on a third-party library, and it does not warn that such libraries need compatibility checks.
recommendations.root_cause: The route assumes a DIA-NN-generated library.
recommendations.fix: Add --fasta (plus --reannotate for third-party libraries) and DIA-NN's advice to prefer DIA-NN-generated .parquet/.speclib libraries.

recommendations.title: Version drift in output and default claims
recommendations.problem: --out-lib uses .tsv although empirical libraries are .parquet since 1.9.1; '--qvalue 0.01 = DIA-NN default' is false for current docs (5%); directDIA and predicted-library are presented as different routes.
recommendations.root_cause: The text mixes 1.8-era conventions with 1.9+ claims.
recommendations.fix: Use .parquet library names, date the default claims by version, and describe library-free search as DIA-NN's predicted-library route.

recommendations.title: Example script fragile and missing promised filter
recommendations.problem: Unquoted --f $f splits filenames with spaces; an empty directory passes a literal '*.mzML'; the header promises filtering but the script only has comments.
recommendations.root_cause: The example was written as illustration, not as a runnable pipeline.
recommendations.fix: Build args with an array (args+=(--f "$f")), check that diann, the FASTA and mzML files exist, and add the Python filter step.
